Hi Olivia / Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Good to hear the FinLytics constraints (air-gapped lab option, strict egress policy, and the desire to avoid an external control-plane dependency). Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages with an optional customer-managed control plane.
- Two deployment patterns: (1) private control plane inside your VPC with mTLS to agents, or (2) fully air-gapped runtime where control plane services are deployed locally (no outbound).
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers: predictable token economics, model pinning/rollouts, built-in KV/prefix caching for steady latency at scale, and explicit offline-control-plane path for regulated setups.

Proposed technical tests (what we suggest next)
1) Network connectivity test (peering & routing) — we’ll validate NAT/firewall rules required for the control-plane pattern.
2) Control-plane isolation test — demonstrate running the control plane inside your VPC (no public endpoints).
3) Air-gap feasibility checklist — a hands-on run of a minimal on-prem package in your lab (no outbound).
4) Load profile smoke run — small end-to-end 10 qps test using one model variant to validate latency and KV cache behavior.

Success criteria we recommend
- Control plane deployed without outbound egress (for the air-gapped trial)
- End-to-end 95th latency < 150ms for 512-token seq at 10 qps (lab profile)
- Model pinning and seamless rollback working from console

Attachments
- redwood-private-vpc-design.pdf (networking diagram + ports checklist)
- hyperscaler-compare-sheet.xlsx (feature/ops/cost comparison)

As next step: can we schedule a 2-hour lab session next week where our infra engineer (Ben) pairs with your Marcus to run tests 1–3? Suggested windows: Tue Aug 11 10:00–12:00 PT or Wed Aug 12 13:00–15:00 PT. If those don't work, suggest two slots that do. Also please confirm the lab VM specs (CPU/GPU/no-GPU) and whether you want us to bring a small GPU node for the load smoke run.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

— Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Looping in technical answers so we can reply to Olivia with specifics: 

1) Outbound telemetry: by default the hosted control-plane ships aggregated metrics to our SaaS telemetry, but for Private customers we offer a "no-telemetry" mode and an option to point metrics at a customer-managed endpoint inside the VPC (or disable entirely). For air-gapped installs the control plane can be configured to write logs locally; we will provide a build that contains zero external telemetry endpoints.

2) Air-gap dependencies: minimal — Python3, systemd, OpenSSL, and our packaged runtime tar with a signed license blob. We'll provide a pre-flight checklist and RPM/deb bundles. No external package manager access is required if you stage the bundles into the lab. I'll attach the checklist to the next message.

3) CPU-only smoke run: useful for functional validation (latency will be slower than GPU but you can validate control-plane behavior, routing, and model pinning). For representative latency numbers we recommend at least one GPU node; however, the lab smoke run still proves the deployment pattern.

Ben — can you draft the minimal firewall/NAT rules we'll need to validate the private control-plane pattern (ports and direction)? I'll consolidate into a short doc for Olivia.

— Aisha
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
